title: Heuristic: Workflow Falsification Audit before deploying any new strategy
rationale: This paper provides a critical methodology hygiene framework. At K=1000 strategy candidates, 100% of in-sample winners are false positives. At K=400, FeatureMining workflows have 100% IS failure rate. The core discipline — running the ENTIRE workflow (preprocessing, feature selection, hyperparameter tuning) against synthetic null environments — is directly applicable before deploying R33 QuantaAlpha or any LLM-mined factor. Key environments: (C) Bid-Ask Bounce Placebo catches timing/execution errors; (D) Factor Null isolates whether alpha is genuinely incremental vs. a disguised known risk premium. The paper's 'effective multiplicity K̂_eff' calculation is essential for multi-strategy searches: 500 correlated strategies may only represent ~5 independent tests, so significance thresholds must be adjusted accordingly. QuantAudit R package forthcoming — monitor for release.
content:
### Workflow Falsification Audit for new factors/strategies
- LESSON: At K=1000 candidate strategies searched, 100% of in-sample 'winners' are statistical artifacts (spurious predictability via adaptive spec search). Before claiming any new factor has alpha, run the workflow against at minimum: (C) Bid-Ask Bounce Placebo and (D) Factor Null environments. A factor that survives null environments has genuine incremental alpha; one that doesn't is an artifact of preprocessing/feature selection contamination.
- LESSON: Effective multiplicity K̂_eff = (Σλ_i)² / Σλ²_i (spectral participation ratio of the strategy correlation matrix). At K=500 correlated strategies, K̂_eff may be as low as 5 — adjust significance threshold accordingly. Never report p-values without accounting for effective multiplicity.
- LESSON: FeatureMining workflows are the most dangerous (100% IS failure rate, ΔZ=2.68 inflation at K=1000). Any LLM-driven feature discovery pipeline that generates 100s of candidate features MUST use strict IS/OOS disjointness — all feature selection must occur only on in-sample data. The QuantAudit R package (GitHub/CRAN, forthcoming) automates this audit.
- WHEN: Before deploying any new mined factor (R33 QuantaAlpha/AlphaPROBE), any new LLM-derived signal (R28 Phase 2, R29 LLM filter), or any backtest where feature engineering was adaptive. Run falsification audit as final gate before claiming Sharpe improvement.
- SOURCE: arXiv:2604.15531 (April 2026) — Spurious Predictability in Financial Machine Learning. Nikolopoulos.
